newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market quiet on reporting day.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market quiet on reporting day.

text.p: Limited trade in government securities marked the reporting day, dealers said on Friday.
Banks do not borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Uncertainty over call money rates in the next fortnight kept market players to the sidelines on Friday, dealers said.
They said market players were waiting to see which way call money rates would move before taking positions in securities.
"At the moment it still appears that call money will be around 10 percent through next fortnight," a dealer said.
"Market players are not willing to lock up funds in securities if rates are this high."
Prices of government securites were laregly steady in limited trade on Friday, dealers said.
Most of the day's deals were in treasury bills with some deals reported in stock maturing in 2004, they said.
Dealers said four-day money was traded between seven percent and 7.5 percent, a dealer said.
"This is an indication that call money will open around ten percent tomorrow," he said.
